title: wb migrate carries a numbered list as one item, while bullets carry one per line
body:
`intent wb migrate` carries a numbered list as one item, while a bulleted list carries one item per bullet.

**Seen 2026-09-19** in Lamplight's whiteboard carry (89ec8c350): ic's four-item numbered TODO became one todo, and hv's two unexecuted rulings of 2026-08-19, written as `1.` and `2.` lines, became one decision with an embedded `2.`, so neither could be archived without the other. `- ` lines carry one per item; `1.` lines do not. Both boards were re-split by hand afterwards (a19193c15).

**The ask:** the carry treats an ordered-list line the way it treats a bullet, one item per line, and the plain pass's report says how many items each section yields so a node can compare it with the list it wrote. S.


CLOSED 2026-09-20, by the landing at 5bce95058ce224a9e32f89b4f2bde7b180464d01, patch-id 96e15ee1dd69e7a85269d326bcd434a3383db836 read back off the committed tree and identical to the judged bank (refs/bank/cc/0488-0489/patch, blob b8cf2491f86a4a7821bee08a8039a5431097e742), banked with 0489 as one change because both move the same classifier.

**What changed.** `wbmigrate::blocks_to_items` learns CommonMark's ordered marker -- one or more DIGITS, then `.` or `)`, then a space. Digits only, ruled by vc 2026-09-20: `a.` and `i.` are not markers, because a lettered list is rare on a board and a sentence opening `A. ` is not, and admitting letters would split prose nobody wrote as a list, which is the expensive direction when the split is what makes each piece an item of work.

**The opener decides the whole block, and a mixed block is not an error.** A `- ` line inside a numbered list is a continuation, and a `1.` line inside a bullet list is too, so an author who mixes markers gets one list rather than two interleaved ones. The bullet branch deliberately keeps `trim_start_matches("- ")` rather than slicing the two bytes: it strips a REPEATED `- `, so `- - x` has always carried as `x`, and changing that here would move carries this issue is not about.

**The report now says what each section yielded**, every kind printed with zeros included. A single total is a number nobody can check: the author of a board knows how many lines they wrote under DOING and cannot know how many items a whole carry should have produced. The zero is the case worth seeing, so printing only the kinds that appeared would hide exactly the section that vanished.

**The control, driven to both verdicts.** With the ordered opener removed and the arm unchanged, `a_numbered_list_carries_one_item_per_line_and_a_mixed_block_follows_its_opener` fails, and its output is this defect verbatim: one item reading `1. the first numbered thing\n2. the second numbered thing\n3) the third, with a paren delimiter\n10. the tenth`, against the four items expected. That is ic's four-item TODO and hv's two rulings, reproduced on demand. With the fix restored, all 11 arms in `wbmigrate_reads_a_board.rs` pass, the 9 that predate this included, so the ordered marker has not disturbed the bullet, prose, empty-section or table behaviour.
